title: Service Desk Team Leader
description:
Paul Mitchell The School Orlando is hiring!

Guest Experience Team Lead - Join Our Team!

We are seeking a motivated and service-driven Guest Experience Team Lead to support daily operations and create an exceptional experience for every guest who walks through our doors. This leadership role is responsible for guiding the Guest Experience Team, supporting smooth guest flow, maintaining service standards, and partnering with school leadership to ensure an outstanding environment for guests, Future Professionals, and team members.

If you are passionate about customer service, enjoy developing others, and thrive in a fast-paced, team-oriented environment, we invite you to apply!

About our School

Each Paul Mitchell school is independently owned and operated and committed to providing a high-quality educational experience. We support Future Professionals, our students, in developing strong technical skills, creativity, professionalism, and a sense of community. Our programs in cosmetology and other state-approved disciplines prepare students to achieve state licensure and pursue their career goals in a collaborative, inclusive, and student-centered learning environment.

Job Summary

The Guest Experience Team Leader is responsible for leading, coordinating, and supporting guest experience operations within the clinic environment. This role ensures consistent execution of guest service standards, oversees front-of-house operations, retail product inventory and display, and provides coaching and support to Guest Experience Team Members. This position focuses on execution, consistency, and people leadership and does not provide licensed instruction, evaluate technical skills, manage budgets, or enforce academic or sanitation compliance.

Essential Functions

  • Lead and coordinate daily guest experience operations to support smooth guest flow and service transitions.
  • Provide coaching, guidance, and support to Guest Experience Team Members.
  • Monitor guest experience execution and escalate operational issues as needed.
  • Support scheduling, coverage, and coordination of guest experience staff.
  • Serve as an escalation point for guest service concerns and ensure timely resolution through appropriate channels.
  • Reinforce approved guest experience systems, standards, and behaviors.
  • Partner with operations and education leadership to align guest flow with clinic and classroom needs.
  • Communicate priorities, observations, and operational needs to leadership.
  • Support opening and closing procedures and ensure guest-facing areas meet presentation standards.
  • Oversee and manage retail products, displays, and shelves.
  • Report product inventory to the School Director.

​Requirements

Education, Licensure, and Experience:

  • High school diploma or equivalent required; additional experience in leadership, hospitality, or service operations preferred
  • Prior experience in guest services, front desk operations, or service-based leadership roles preferred

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

  • Ability to coach and support team members effectively
  • Strong oral and written communication, organization, and problem-solving skills
  • Ability to balance guest service priorities with operational needs
  • Working knowledge of scheduling, point-of-sale, and guest management systems
  • Ability to maintain professionalism and composure in a fast-paced environment

Schedule Expectations

This role is performed primarily on-site at the school location. No remote work is available for this position.

Work schedules vary by location and role, based on operational need, and may include:

  • Daytime, evening, or weekend hours based on the school's program schedule
  • Occasional mandatory weekend days
  • Occasional school events, outreach, or activities outside of standard hours

Paul Mitchell The School Orlando is an equal opportunity employer.


NOTICE OF NON-DISCRIMINATION: Paul Mitchell The School Orlando ("School") does not discriminate on the basis of protected class status, including sex, and prohibits sex discrimination in any education program or activity that it operates as required by Title IX and its regulations, including in admission and employment. Inquiries about Title IX may be referred to the School's Title IX Coordinator, the U.S. Department of Civil Rights, or both. The School's Title IX Coordinator is: T'meda Holt, 1285 Oviedo Mall Blvd., Oviedo, FL 32765 p: (407) 677-7695 Ext 2107, e: t'meda@orlando.paulmitchell.edu

The School's Protected Class Non-Discrimination Policy and Grievance Procedures can be located here https://paul-mitchell-schools-website-lightsail.s3.amazonaws.com/uploads/sites/213/Orlando-Protected-Class-Non-Discrimination-Policy-and-Procedures_10312. To Report information about conduct that may constitute sex discrimination or make a complaint of sex discrimination under Title IX, please contact the Title IX Coordinator through one of the above methods (telephone, email, or in person at their office).

Since 1997, Apex IT our Salesforce and Oracle experts have provided a full range of enterprise solutions including CRM and related applications that support sales, marketing, and service; financial reporting; HR; and Business Intelligence. As a remote company, we have top talent all over the United States and India and are continuously growing. We provide our team with a flexible work-life balance in addition to the traditional benefits.

About Apex IT:

Apex IT is a global consulting firm that provides award-winning services to transform customer, employee, and student experiences. Our Salesforce and Oracle experts understand the transformative power of Salesforce and Oracle platforms in driving business growth and success. We guide businesses through the entire Salesforce implementation process, from planning and configuration to customization and integration. We provide end-to-end consulting, implementation, and migration services for Oracle Cloud applications. Whether it's Oracle CX, HCM, ERP, SCM, or EPM, our experts help businesses leverage the power of the cloud to enhance agility, scalability, and cost-efficiency.

In addition to consulting, our digital marketing agency, Apex Theorem, focuses on driving digital transformation. Our Marketing Acceleration Advisors create proprietary, results-driven solutions that increase lead conversion, enhance customer engagement, and drive revenue growth.

With our headquarters in the US and a strong business unit in India, we are excited to announce our expansion into Colombia. This expansion will allow us to leverage Colombia's growing tech talent pool, strengthening our capabilities and positioning us for an even greater impact.

Job Title: HCM Product Owner

Classification: Exempt under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA)

Reports to: President

Work Location/Travel: Work is remote or on-site. Percentage of travel, where the travel occurs, such as locally or in specific countries or states, and whether the travel is overnight, varies. This resource must be willing and able to travel as required by the customer project.

Job Summary: The HCM Product Owner is responsible for the functional support, enhancement, and strategic roadmap of Oracle HCM Cloud applications, including Core HR, Payroll, Benefits, Absence Management, Time and Labor, Talent Management, Recruiting, and Workforce Management. This role serves as the primary liaison between HR, Payroll, Finance, IT, and business stakeholders to ensure HCM solutions effectively support business operations, compliance requirements, and employee experience objectives. The HCM Product Owner manages business priorities, oversees system enhancements, resolves complex functional issues, and drives continuous improvement of HCM processes. This position is responsible for developing the Oracle HCM roadmap, evaluating emerging capabilities including AI-enabled solutions, and ensuring alignment with enterprise architecture, cross-functional business processes, and organizational goals.

Essential Functions:

  • Serve as the Product Owner for Oracle HCM Cloud applications, including Core HR, Payroll, Benefits, Absence Management, Time and Labor, Talent Management, Recruiting, and Workforce Management.
  • Develop, maintain, and communicate the Oracle HCM product roadmap, aligning initiatives with business objectives and enterprise architecture.
  • Partner with HR, Payroll, Finance, IT, and business stakeholders to identify, prioritize, and deliver system enhancements and process improvements.
  • Manage and prioritize the HCM product backlog, including requirements gathering, user stories, testing, and release activities.
  • Provide functional leadership and support for Oracle HCM processes, including payroll processing, employee lifecycle events, benefits administration, time entry, approvals, position management, and compliance-related activities.
  • Analyze and resolve complex functional issues while ensuring system stability, performance, and user satisfaction.
  • Evaluate Oracle quarterly releases, new functionality, and emerging technologies to identify opportunities for business value and operational efficiencies.
  • Lead user acceptance testing, business readiness, and transition activities to support successful implementation of new capabilities.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to ensure HCM solutions integrate effectively with Finance, Payroll, and related enterprise systems.
  • Establish and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) to measure system effectiveness, adoption, process efficiency, and business outcomes.
  • Support data governance, reporting, compliance, and audit requirements related to HCM processes and employee data.
  • Identify opportunities to leverage AI-enabled HCM capabilities, automation, and self-service tools to improve employee and manager experiences.
  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives that simplify processes, enhance data quality, and increase operational effectiveness.
  • Provide subject matter expertise and strategic guidance regarding Oracle HCM capabilities, best practices, and future-state solutions.

Duties/Responsibilities:

  • Maintain and pursue continuing education opportunities, such as training and certification exams.
  • Participate on internal projects.
  • Provide expertise and help to others, as needed, on projects.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.

Competency:

  • Thorough understanding of information technology procedures and practices.
  • Flexible to changing needs.
  • Organized with attention to detail.
  • Good at follow-up
  • Willingness to get hands on with the product.
  • Works well with a team
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills
  • Excellent analytical, logical thinking, and problem-solving skills.
  • Thorough understanding of HCM principles and planning.
  • Proficient with, or able to quickly become proficient with, a range of general and specialized applications, software, and hardware used in the organization and the industry.
  • Proficient with Microsoft Office Suite or related software.

Supervisory Responsibilities:

  • May assist with training members of the technical staff.
  • May conduct interviews.
  • Assigns duties and responsibilities and oversees workflow of project staff.
  • May conduct project performance evaluations that are timely and constructive.

Work Environment:

The work environment is remote or on-site at a client location. While remote, employees are expected to provide office space for themselves with a professional background (including virtual backgrounds) and noise level. A reliable and consistent internet connection is required.

Physical Requirements:

  • Prolonged periods sitting or standing at a desk and working on a computer.
  • Bending, sitting lifting, driving.

Position Type and expected hours of work:

  • Full time work during Apex IT business hours and, at times, outside of business hours, if required.

Required Education and Experience:

  • Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Information Systems, Business Administration, Computer Science, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience required.
  • At least 5 years of experience supporting or managing Oracle HCM Cloud applications required.
  • Experience with multiple Oracle HCM modules, including Core HR, Payroll, Benefits, Absence, Time and Labor, Talent Management, Recruiting, and Workforce Management required.

Preferred Education and Experience:

  • Oracle HCM Cloud certifications preferred.
  • Experience serving as a Product Owner, Business Analyst, or Functional Lead preferred.
  • Experience with HCM transformation, system implementations, or major enhancement projects preferred.
  • Knowledge of AI-enabled HCM capabilities, workforce analytics, and process automation preferred.

Other Duties:

This job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties, or responsibilities that are required. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change, or new ones may be assigned at any time, with or without notice.

title: Telehealth Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA)
description:
FronteraCare delivers life-changing autism services to children and families across New Mexico and Colorado. We provide high quality diagnostic evaluations and ABA therapy, partnering closely with parents, grandparents, foster parents, and other caregivers to create individualized care plans rooted in each child's unique strengths, needs, and family context.

Our clinicians are committed to evidence-based, compassionate care that helps children with autism thrive. We believe the best outcomes are when families are at the heart of the treatment. By combining clinical expertise with family insights, we help children build skills, gain confidence, and thrive.

Our Mission
Our mission is to expand access to exceptional diagnostic and behavioral healthcare for every child, no matter where they live or their circumstances.

About the Role:

At FronteraCare, we’re not just providing ABA therapy, we’re transforming how behavioral health is delivered. Born from firsthand experience with the delays and inefficiencies in today’s diagnostic and therapeutic systems, FronteraCare was created to bridge the gap between families and the care they need. We do this by combining compassionate, culturally informed clinical care with innovative technology that supports—rather than replaces—clinicians, making care more precise, accessible, and sustainable.

We’re seeking a mission-driven, technology-forward Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA) to join our telehealth team in New Mexico. This is more than a clinical role, it’s a leadership opportunity. As a BCBA at Frontera, you’ll be at the forefront of an innovative care model that leverages digital phenotyping, intelligent assessment tools, and asynchronous supervision technology to expand access and improve outcomes. You’ll lead and mentor RBTs with intention, ensuring high-quality implementation and meaningful professional development.

If you believe in the power of technology to transform care—without compromising clinical integrity, and if you're passionate about guiding and growing the next generation of behavior technicians, we want to hear from you.

The BCBA will operate within Local, State and Federal Regulations as well as adhere to all Frontera policies and procedures. Essential duties include but are not limited to:

  • Conducting behavior or functional Analytic Assessment Process
  • Developing the case supervision and clinical management
  • Developing and implementing an ABA Treatment Plan
  • Consulting with a Registered Behavior Technicians (RBT) or Behavior Technicians (BT) regarding client/family concerns
  • Selecting appropriate stimulus materials and treatment modalities for age and ability of person served
  • Including the client/family in setting treatment goals and training families on specific treatment strategies and carryover skills for the client/family
  • Giving clear concise instructions in presenting materials and/or techniques in therapy
  • Recording and tracking daily progress for client/family accurately
  • Utilizing time in session efficiently to meet objectives
  • Providing accurate and immediate feedback to the client and/or family
  • Planning for discharge of the person served

General Requirements:

  • General knowledge and experience in the field of Applied Behavior Analysis
  • Services and/or knowledge of Autism Spectrum Disorder
  • Managerial experience
  • Proficient computer skills in Excel, database management and record keeping.
  • Effective oral and written communication.
  • Excellent interpersonal and coaching skills.
  • Evidence of the practice of a high level of confidentiality.
  • Excellent organizational skills.
  • Completing stage two assessments
  • Completing other duties as assigned

Education and Experience:

  • BCBA (Board Certified Assistant Behavior Analyst) certification.
  • Master's Degree in Psychology or related field, emphasis in Applied Behavior Analysis.
  • Two or more years of experience working with a pediatric population.
  • Two or more years of experience in an applied setting participating in functional assessments/analyses, the development and implementation of functional behavior plans as well as the ongoing oversight and monitoring of the implementation and adjustments to such programs.
  • Memberships to specific state and national (ABAI) professional associations are highly recommended.
  • 1+ year of Telehealth supervision experience
  • Located in NM, AZ, TX, FL, GA, ID, NC, NV, UT, OK, or CO
  • Ability to work within the hours of 9am-6pm MT

Compensation: Compensation for this role is hourly W2, with rates determined based on factors such as experience, geographic location, and language capabilities. On average, compensation for this position is equivalent to approximately $100,000 annually, though individual compensation will vary based on qualifications and other factors.

Join us in building the future of developmental healthcare!

At FronteraCare, we're committed to innovation in the ABA field. We’re excited to offer clinicians access to our cutting-edge Assessment Builder, the first platform that leverages AI, computer vision, and clinical reasoning to analyze unstructured data. If you're looking to streamline your workflow, save time, and leverage cutting-edge AI, this is it! Learn more and give it a try here.

Why Join Us
At Frontera Care, you will be part of a mission-driven, supportive team making a real difference for children and families. We provide the tools, resources, collaboration you need to focus on what matters most: delivering high-quality, family-centered care. If you are passionate about helping children with autism, and want to grow your career while transforming access to care, accessible healthcare, we would love to welcome you to our team.

title: SPL EMEA Agent
description:
Before you apply to a job, select your language preference from the options available at the top right of this page.

Explore your next opportunity at a Fortune Global 500 organization. Envision innovative possibilities, experience our rewarding culture, and work with talented teams that help you become better every day. We know what it takes to lead UPS into tomorrow—people with a unique combination of skill + passion. If you have the qualities and drive to lead yourself or teams, there are roles ready to cultivate your skills and take you to the next level.

Job Description:

Job Title: GBS Agent

Job Summary

This position is responsible for monitoring and executing the day-to-day operations of the SPL EMEA team.

Team provides 24 X 7 support for multiple internal and customer support channels providing order fulfillment. This includes coordinating transportation of real-time inventory through multiple organizations and courier networks, investigating service issues, and resolving customer inquiries.

Administrative staff will play a vital role in supporting core operational teams by managing documentation workflows, maintaining accurate system records, coordinating internal communications, and ensuring timely completion of administrative tasks that underpin customer-facing operations.

The Agent supports efficient and timely service delivery by managing SBD/NBD tasks, providing 24/7 first‑line support, and executing both front‑office and back‑office operational activities. The role ensures accurate order handling, effective customer communication, and reliable reporting, enabling operational teams to focus on higher‑complexity and customer‑impacting tasks.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Manage Same Business Day (SBD) and Next Business Day (NBD) workflows to meet service standards.
  • Provide 24/7/365 first‑line operational support for in‑hours and out‑of‑hours requests.
  • Handle customer calls/emails and execute end‑to‑end order management through to closure.
  • Track shipments and drive timely issue resolution in coordination with internal teams.
  • Act as a foundational support function that enables operational teams to focus on higher‑complexity, customer‑impacting work.

Qualifications:

  • Proven experience working in environments with a strong emphasis on efficiency, organization, and task management (UPS experience preferred)
  • Fluent in English with excellent verbal and written communication skills
  • Knowledge of shipping and logistics solutions and a solution-oriented mindset
  • Highly organized, detail-oriented, and able to manage multiple tasks in a project-driven environment
  • Quick learner with strong follow-through and problem-solving skills
  • Strong collaboration skills and ability to work effectively with internal partners across functions
  • Experience using customer success platforms (e.g., Salesforce) and making data-driven decisions


Employee Type:

Permanent


UPS is committed to providing a workplace free of discrimination, harassment, and retaliation.

title: Oceanarium Director
description:
All Job Postings will close at 12:01 a.m. CT on the specified Closing Date (if designated).

Working Title:

Oceanarium Director

Institution:

Minnesota State University, Moorhead

Classification Title:

MSUAASF Range C

Bargaining Unit / Union:

211: Minnesota State University Association of Administrative Service Faculty

City:

Moorhead

FLSA:

Non Job Exempt

Full Time / Part Time:

Part time

Employment Condition:

Unclassified - Limited Academic (Fixed Term)

Salary Range:

$47,845.00 - $93,809.00

Position Purpose:
The Oceanarium Facility Coordinator has three main areas of responsibility: (1) Maintain the Oceanarium facility to safeguard the health and welfare of the marine organisms that live there, and (2) supervise BIOL 130/230/330 Oceanarium interns in the basics of life support systems in an oceanarium facility, specialized feeding needs of all the organisms, maintenance of water quality and filtration needs, and (3) coordinate, lead and supervise use of the oceanarium for MSUM courses, tours for prospective students by Admissions, outreach tours or K12, Open Hours and special events for the public, and support student interns in the teaching of Junior Aquarists Camp for Kids (JACK workshop in College for Kids).

Responsibilities:
1. Maintenance of the oceanarium facility: Coordinate maintenance of facility, husbandry of marine organisms, maintain water quality [make water, water changes, change socks, clean filters and pumps], maintain and repair oceanarium equipment. Oceanarium Facility Coordinator does simple maintenance and repair, acts as liaison with manufacturers and/or MSUM Physical Plant to coordinate specialized procedures such as plumbing and electrical work.
Priority: Essential Percent of Time: 30%

2. Leads the work of student workers and volunteers to aid in facility maintenance such as monitoring water quality and animal health, animal feeding. Supervises the internship experience of BIOL 130/230/330 Oceanarium students. Create schedule, assign tasks and monitor feeding schedule, sock replacements, daily water top-offs, glass cleaning.
Priority: Essential Percent of Time: 30%

3. Develop content and present public tours of the oceanarium. Hire, train, and supervise student workers, O.C.E.A.N. volunteers and students in BIOL 130/230/330 Oceanarium to aid in public education such as leading tours and engaging the public with information about diversity and conservation of marine ecosystems.
Priority: Essential Percent of Time: 30%

4. Coordinate use of Oceanarium with other outreach efforts at MSUM (Planetarium, Regional Science Center, College for Kids, Dragon Ambassadors for Admissions tours), and other community partners in public education such as the Red River Zoo, and Science Museum.
Priority: Essential Percent of Time: 5%

5. Ongoing professional development.

  • Expand your professional development network by attending conferences within the field
  • Stay current on the latest trends, technologies, and best practices.
  • Develop new skills by participating in virtual and hands-on training opportunities.

Priority: Essential Percent of Time: 5%

6.Be sensitive in dealings with other personnel, visitors, and students, so that all are treated in a respectful and professional manner. Be respectful of and sensitive to the rights, responsibilities and duties of others, and respectful of the human rights of all racial, ethic, and religious groups, including protected groups as defined by state statute. Maintain professional level of conduct and interaction with other staff so that staff dissension is minimized. Maintain control and composure during difficult and stressful situations to instill a calming effect on others. Maintain a professional distance in relationships with students and their families.
Priority: Essential Percent of Time: 100%

Salary Range:
$47,845.00 - $93,809.00 USD Annual

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Master’s degree in a marine biology, science education, or similar field - or -
  • Bachelor’s degree plus one year of professional experience running a marine facility - or - Two years of professional experience or an equivalent combination of post-secondary training, education and/or professional experience running a marine educational facility.
  • •General understanding of marine animal husbandry, water chemistry, filtration systems
  • Ability to maintain the Oceanarium
  • Organizational ability
  • Ability to supervise students and volunteers
  • Ability to help academic departments integrate the Oceanarium into their curricula
  • Ability to coordinate with other members of CSHE outreach efforts
  • Ability to oversee development of educational content for MSUM, K-12 and public audiences
  • Ability to oversee budget

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Master’s degree in marine biology, science education, or similar field
  • Experience maintaining a large public marine aquarium facility
  • Experience in K12 community outreach relating to marine ecosystem ecology and conservation
  • Experience supervising student workers
  • Demonstrated ability to plan and develop future directions for a facility such as the oceanarium
  • Demonstrated ability to coordinate outreach efforts with other forms of science outreach

Other Requirements:
The successful candidate must be able to lawfully accept employment in the United States by the day employment begins. The University regrets that we are unable to offer H-1B sponsorship at this time.

A completed application will include a resume and cover letter.

Work Shift (Hours / Days of work)

This is a Fixed-Term, Monday - Friday position and is a 0.75 FTE

Telework: No

About:
Minnesota State Moorhead is a vibrant community that pushes you to forge your own path. Help shape a campus where students thrive, connect, and lead!


Benefits Information:

At Minnesota State, we take your well-being and work-life balance seriously. We offer a comprehensive benefits package that features low-cost medical and dental insurance with affordable deductibles, employer-paid life insurance, short- and long-term disability, and pre-tax healthcare and dependent care accounts with a roll-over option. To further support your holistic health, employees also have access to a confidential Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for mental health, legal, and financial counseling. Detailed plan details, rates, and coverage choices can be reviewed directly via the State Employee Group Insurance Program (SEGIP) website.

To support your life outside of work, our package includes 12 paid holidays, generous vacation and sick time, and six weeks of Paid Parental Leave. We also help you secure your financial future with a robust Pension Plan, 457(b) and 403(b) retirement accounts, and various investment options. Furthermore, we invest in your growth by providing dedicated professional development and tuition waivers for both you and your dependents. Please note that specific benefit eligibility and coverage levels may vary depending on the type of position, employee classification, and collective bargaining agreements.

title: Assistant Golf Professional
description:
We invite you to join the world of luxury hospitality at Fairmont Grand Del Mar, as our new Assistant Golf Professional.

The Assistant Golf Professional is responsible for supporting the daily golf operation and delivering an exceptional experience for members and guests. This role assists in overseeing tee sheet management, golf shop operations, retail sales, instructional programming, tournament execution, and service standards while maintaining alignment with the luxury standards of Fairmont Grand Del Mar and The Grand Golf Club. The Assistant Golf Professional serves as a key operational leader and ambassador of the Club, ensuring efficient daily execution, strong communication across departments, and a high level of personalized service.

Responsibilities

  • Serve as a representative of The Grand Golf Club and Fairmont Grand Del Mar by displaying professionalism, discretion, courtesy, and hospitality in all interactions with members, guests, vendors, and colleagues.
  • Maintain and uphold departmental service standards, operating procedures, and presentation expectations at all times.
  • Assist with daily golf operations including tee sheet management, point-of-sale transactions, reservations, and guest check-in procedures.
  • Manage daily play through tee sheet and POS systems, ensuring accuracy of billing, guest information, and tee time details.
  • Handle phone inquiries, reservations, and member/guest requests with professionalism and attention to detail.
  • Communicate daily operational priorities, special events, member notes, and relevant information to the Player Services team, Golf Leadership team, and other departments as needed.
  • Work closely with Player Services to coordinate guest arrivals, golf cart assignments, bag handling, and on-course needs.
  • Act as Player Host, Starter, or practice facility support as assigned.
  • Support golf shop retail operations including merchandising standards, stock organization, product knowledge, and special orders.
  • Assist Golf Merchandiser with maintaining shop presentation, merchandising displays, stock replenishment, and monthly physical inventory counts.
  • Maintain knowledge of current retail vendors, apparel sizing, hard goods, and special-order processes.
  • Conduct private instruction, group clinics, club fitting sessions, and player development programs.
  • Demonstrate proficiency with instructional and fitting technologies including Coach Now and the like, SAM PuttLab, launch monitors, and current fitting/demo equipment.
  • Support tournament operations, scoring, and event execution utilizing Golf Genius software.
  • Assist with member events, corporate outings, clinics, and other golf programming as assigned.
  • Coordinate forecaddie communication and scheduling support when needed.
  • Support operations in all golf department areas including Golf Shop, practice facilities, Player Services, and Members Locker Room as needed.
  • Build relationships with members through regular engagement and personalized service, including playing golf with members when appropriate and operationally feasible.
  • Maintain PGA education progress and participate in applicable Chapter, Section, and Association meetings, education seminars, and professional development opportunities.
  • Ensure compliance with all company safety standards, operational procedures, and ongoing training requirements.
  • Perform additional duties as assigned by Golf Leadership.

  • High school diploma or equivalent required; college degree preferred.
  • Previous golf operations or hospitality experience required, preferably in a private club, resort, or high-end daily fee environment.
  • PGA Associate (Level 1 or higher required) or PGA Member in good standing.
  • Strong computer proficiency including POS systems, tee sheet management software, Microsoft Office, and golf-related technology platforms.
  • Experience with tournament software, retail operations, and instructional technology preferred.
  • Strong organizational skills with ability to prioritize multiple tasks in a fast-paced environment.
  • Excellent communication, interpersonal, and service recovery skills.
  • Ability to lead, direct, and collaborate with hourly staff and cross-functional teams.
  • Positive, enthusiastic, professional, and team-oriented attitude.
  • Must develop strong familiarity with members, including preferences and service expectations.
  • Valid driver’s license and ability to operate golf carts and club vehicles safely.
  • Ability to obtain required food and alcohol certifications as applicable.
  • Availability to work a flexible schedule including mornings, evenings, weekends, holidays, and occasional overnight or special event shifts.

Physical Demands

  • Ability to stand and walk for extended periods of time.
  • Ability to sit, bend, kneel, squat, twist, and reach frequently throughout the shift.
  • Ability to lift, carry, push, and pull up to 50 pounds.
  • Ability to work indoors and outdoors in varying weather conditions for extended periods.
  • Frequent use of golf carts, computer systems, telephones, and standard office equipment.
  • Ability to safely operate golf-related equipment and department vehicles.
  • Use of required protective equipment and adherence to all safety protocols.

Assistant Golf Professional Tier Structure

  • Tier 3: PGA Associate Level 1 & 2
  • Tier 2: PGA Associate Level 3
  • Tier 1: PGA Class A Member

Wage Information

The hourly rate for this position is $23.00 - $25.00/hour USD depending on experience

Job Perks & Benefits: Join our team and enjoy a range of exclusive colleague perks, including complimentary upgrades, extended stays, discounted stays across Fairmont & Raffles properties, special dining and wellness discounts, and added luxuries to enhance your experience. We believe in taking care of our team, ensuring that your hard work is rewarded with exceptional benefits.

What is in it for you:

  • Complimentary Meals: Enjoy hot meals during your shift in our staff cafeteria
  • Complimentary on-site parking
  • Hotel Discounts: Employee travel program with discounts on room rates at Fairmont & Accor properties world-wide.
  • Food, Spa, and Resort Discounts: Employee program with discounts on restaurants, bars and spa services at Fairmont & Accor properties world-wide.
  • Career Growth Around the World: Opportunity to develop your talent and grow within Fairmont Grand Del Mar and over 5,700 properties with Accor.
  • Training & Development: Learning programs through our Academies designed to sharpen your skills
  • Social Responsibility: Ability to make a difference through our Corporate Social Responsibility activities
  • Recognition & Rewards: Employees are recognized for outstanding performance through appreciation programs, awards, and exclusive travel and lifestyle perks.
  • Meaningful Work: Create memorable experiences for guests while making a positive impact through exceptional hospitality and service.

Health and Retirement Benefits

All full-time employees are eligible for our comprehensive benefits package, which includes:

  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance (effective the first of the month following 30 days of employment)
  • Eligible single Full-Time employees can enroll in a $0 premium health plan
  • Life and disability insurance
  • Paid Holidays

All Full-time and Part-time employees are eligible for:

  • Vacation and sick leave
  • 401(k) retirement plan with matching program
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

Diversity & Inclusion

Fairmont is committed to creating an inclusive environment where diverse talent thrives. We welcome candidates from all backgrounds to join our team.

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

Visa Requirements: Applicants must be legally eligible to work the United States.

title: BCBA - Parent-Implemented ABA Bilingual (English/Spanish)
description:
FronteraCare delivers life-changing autism services to children and families across New Mexico and Colorado. We provide high quality diagnostic evaluations and ABA therapy, partnering closely with parents, grandparents, foster parents, and other caregivers to create individualized care plans rooted in each child's unique strengths, needs, and family context.

Our clinicians are committed to evidence-based, compassionate care that helps children with autism thrive. We believe the best outcomes are when families are at the heart of the treatment. By combining clinical expertise with family insights, we help children build skills, gain confidence, and thrive.

Our Mission
Our mission is to expand access to exceptional diagnostic and behavioral healthcare for every child, no matter where they live or their circumstances.

Position Overview

We are seeking a Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA) who is passionate about expanding access to high-quality, caregiver-mediated ABA services. This role focuses on delivering parent-implemented interventions through telehealth, equipping caregivers with the skills and confidence to support meaningful progress in their child’s natural environment.

This BCBA will partner closely with families to model, coach, and reinforce evidence-based strategies in real time. The role may also contribute to innovative service delivery models, including digital tools and asynchronous supports, to enhance caregiver engagement and continuity of care.

This position is ideal for a BCBA who values a collaborative, family-centered approach, is skilled in translating clinical concepts into practical strategies, and thrives in a flexible, tech-enabled environment.

Key Responsibilities

  • Conduct behavioral and functional analytic assessments with a focus on identifying caregiver strengths, needs, and opportunities for intervention within daily routines
  • Develop and oversee individualized, caregiver-mediated ABA treatment plans that prioritize functional, meaningful outcomes and natural environment teaching
  • Coach, model, and provide real-time feedback to caregivers to support effective implementation of intervention strategies
  • Collaborate with families to set meaningful, achievable goals and build caregiver competence and confidence in supporting their child’s development
  • Monitor client and caregiver progress, adjust treatment plans, and ensure data-driven decision-making using caregiver-collected and session-based data
  • Translate clinical concepts into clear, practical guidance that can be consistently implemented by caregivers in everyday settings
  • Maintain accurate and timely documentation of services, caregiver progress, and client outcomes
  • Plan for generalization, maintenance, and appropriate discharge by ensuring caregivers can independently implement key strategies
  • Ensure compliance with all local, state, and federal regulations, as well as organizational policies and procedures

General Requirements

  • Strong knowledge and experience in Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) and Autism Spectrum Disorder
  • Demonstrated ability to provide clinical supervision and mentorship
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate clearly and concisely in a chat-based format
  • Strong interpersonal, coaching, and relationship-building skills
  • High level of organization, attention to detail, and ability to manage multiple priorities
  • Proficiency with technology, including data systems, telehealth platforms, and digital tools
  • Commitment to maintaining confidentiality and ethical standards
  • Located in NM, AZ, TX, FL, GA, ID, NC, NV, UT, OK, or CO
  • Ability to work within the hours of 9am-6pm MT
  • Bilingual English/Spanish

Education and Experience

  • Active BCBA certification
  • Master’s degree in Psychology, Applied Behavior Analysis, or a related field
  • Minimum of 5 years of experience working with a pediatric population
  • Minimum of 3 years of experience conducting functional assessments and developing and overseeing behavior intervention plans
  • At least 1 year of telehealth supervision experience

Compensation: Compensation for this role is hourly W2, with rates determined based on factors such as experience, geographic location, and language capabilities. On average, compensation for this position is equivalent to approximately $100,000 annually, though individual compensation will vary based on qualifications and other factors.

Why Join Us
At Frontera Care, you will be part of a mission-driven, supportive team making a real difference for children and families. We provide the tools, resources, collaboration you need to focus on what matters most: delivering high-quality, family-centered care. If you are passionate about helping children with autism, and want to grow your career while transforming access to care, accessible healthcare, we would love to welcome you to our team.
